questions.prompt: Why is the 'as ExportData' cast not a check, and what makes validateImport a stronger contract than a boolean validator?

keyPoints.text: Static types vanish before the code runs.
keyPoints.quote: TypeScript types are erased at compile time

keyPoints.text: The cast compiles to the identical JavaScript as the bare JSON.parse call.
validateImport plays the role of the ExportData type at runtime.
keyPoints.quote: is the runtime version of the

keyPoints.text: Taking unknown forces the function to prove each field before touching it.
keyPoints.quote: every property must be checked before use

keyPoints.text: As an assertion function it has exactly two outcomes.
keyPoints.quote: it either throws or returns normally

keyPoints.text: Unlike a returned boolean, the verdict cannot be dropped on the floor.
keyPoints.quote: a caller cannot forget to look at the result

keyPoints.text: Invalid data is stopped at the call boundary itself.
keyPoints.quote: a bad payload never gets past the call

questions.prompt: How do the validator's internal choices - the day helper, first-failure reporting, and size caps - shape what a user learns about a bad backup?

keyPoints.text: Date.parse alone is too forgiving: V8 accepts impossible calendar dates by rolling them forward.
The day helper therefore round-trips the value and demands equality.
keyPoints.quote: formats the parsed date back and requires it to equal the input

keyPoints.text: Validation stops at the first failure and reports coarsely.
keyPoints.quote: names only the block, not the record

keyPoints.text: With thousands of records, that coarseness has a real cost for the user.
keyPoints.quote: learns that one is bad but not which one

keyPoints.text: The array caps are a responsiveness guard, not a domain rule.
keyPoints.quote: stop a huge file from freezing the tab

keyPoints.text: Duplicate card ids are caught by a Set accumulated across the states loop.

questions.prompt: Explain the validate-then-transact structure of importData, its filter-don't-fail policy for unknown cards, and the schema-version stance.

keyPoints.text: A malformed file never reaches storage, so there is nothing to roll back.
The transaction exists for a different failure class than validation.
keyPoints.quote: failures that have nothing to do with the data

keyPoints.text: Relying on the transaction alone would accept structurally fine but wrong data.
Bundled cards absent from the backup are given brand-new states.
keyPoints.quote: creating fresh states for bundled cards the backup did not mention

keyPoints.text: Deck ids, unlike card ids, are not domain-checked at all.
keyPoints.quote: The validator only checks that they are strings

keyPoints.text: Rejecting every other schema version is honest while no migration exists.
keyPoints.quote: a version-0 file has an unknown shape

keyPoints.text: The future pattern is stepwise migration followed by the current validator.
keyPoints.quote: upgrades one version at a time and then calls the current validator
